correctness.rationale: For selected side sizes a,b and d selected missing-matching edges, the induced edge count is ab-d with d<=min(a,b,t). Any 3-by-3 or 2-by-4 selection contains a six-vertex subgraph with at least six edges, hence a cycle. Among 2-by-2 selections, precisely one or two removed matching edges yield P4 and 2K2, respectively; among 2-by-3 selections, exactly two yield P5. Remaining one-small-side cases are stars with possibly one isolate. Count these disjoint categories, correcting 1-by-1 double counting, to derive the full bivariate polynomial. The path, feedback-set and crown endpoint claims follow from its support/coefficient comparison. Exhaustive stdlib verification checked 163 parameter triples and 413040 vertex subsets through p,q<=7; no finite test is asserted to prove all n.

value.rationale: Deleting a natural matching from a complete bipartite graph changes the induced-forest structure in a sharply constrained way. This exact natural three-parameter bivariate enumeration refines feedback-vertex-set cardinalities by all component strata, counts the minimal deletion solutions, and proves a P4-versus-P5 path balance criterion that detects the crown endpoint for any balanced nonzero matching deletion. It is a complete infinite-family classification rather than a routine substitution or isolated small computation.
